headlines.title: Q3 Earnings Preview Might Change The Case For Investing In Charter Communications (CHTR)
headlines.summary: Charter Communications recently renewed Adeia's multi year intellectual property license for Spectrum's video, broadband and mobility services, and also shifted former Chief Commercial Officer Adam Ray into a non executive advisory role through December 31, 2026.

headlines.title: Charter Communications (CHTR) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Cut As Broadband Pressure Weighs
headlines.summary: The fair value estimate for Charter Communications has been adjusted from US$178.05 to US$173.17, reflecting a more conservative view of what the stock may be worth under current assumptions. This shift is consistent with mixed analyst commentary, where pressure on broadband growth and pricing is weighing on sentiment, even as some still see potential value if execution improves and industry conditions stabilize.

headlines.title: Charter Communications (CHTR) Loses Its Commercial Chief, Is The 64% Undervaluation Case Convincing?
headlines.summary: Charter Communications (CHTR) moved as investors digested the news that Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer Adam Ray exited the role on 12 October and shifted into a non-executive advisory post through year end. At a share price of $105.14, Charter Communications reflects a 1 month share price return that is down 25.5% and a year to date share price return that has fallen 49.8%, while the 1 year total shareholder return is down 58.8%.

headlines.title: Charter Communications (CHTR) Chief Commercial Officer Adam Ray Is Stepping Down
headlines.summary: Charter Communications (NasdaqGS:CHTR) announced that Adam Ray is stepping down as Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer. Ray is expected to transition out of the EVP and CCO role while continuing to support Charter in an advisory capacity. The company plans for Ray to remain as an advisor until the end of the year to support commercial leadership and client relationships.

headlines.title: Charter Communications’ Q3 2026 Earnings: What to Expect
headlines.summary: Charter Communications is slated to release its third-quarter results later next month, with analysts forecasting strong double-digit earnings growth.

description: Charter Communications, Inc. operates as a broadband connectivity company in the United States. The company offers subscription-based internet, mobile, video, and voice services; broadband connectivity services, including fixed internet, WiFi, and mobile; Spectrum internet products; advanced WiFi services; and in-home WiFi, which provides customers with high performance wireless routers and managed WiFi services to enhance their wireless internet experience. It also offers wireline voice communications services using voice over internet protocol technology; Call Guard, an advanced caller ID and robocall blocking solution; video programming and video services, including access to an interactive programming guide with parental controls, video on demand and pay-per-view services; and broadband communications solutions, such as internet access, data networking, fiber connectivity, video entertainment, and business telephone services. In addition, the company provides advertising services on cable television networks, various streaming services, and advertising platforms for local, regional and national businesses. Further, it offers production and technical services for regional sports networks; owns and manages local news channels, including Spectrum News NY1® and Spectrum News SoCal; and delivers broadband connectivity solutions to apartments, single-family gated communities, off-campus student housing, senior residences, and RV parks. The company was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.
